landmarks.name: MacOdrum Library
facts: It is the main library, at the heart of campus.
It was one of the first three buildings, built in 1959 around a quadrangle with the Tory Building and Paterson Hall.

landmarks.name: Loeb Building
facts: Arthur Kroeger College has had its offices on its first floor since 1999.

landmarks.name: Tory Building
facts: It is named after the founding president of the University of Alberta, who also led the National Research Council.
It was one of the first three buildings, built in 1959 with the library and Paterson Hall.

landmarks.name: Southam Hall
facts: It is named after a member of a newspaper-publishing family.

landmarks.name: The Minto Centre for Advanced Studies in Engineering
St. Patrick's Building
facts: Since 1992 it has housed the Carleton University Art Gallery at the north end of campus.

landmarks.name: Paterson Hall
facts: It was one of the first three buildings on the Rideau River campus, built in 1959.

landmarks.name: Dunton Tower
facts: It is the tallest building on campus and one of the tallest in Ottawa.
It was finished in September 1972 as the Arts Tower and later named after a former university president.

landmarks.name: Carleton Ice House
facts: Germany's women's national hockey team trained here before the 2013 world championship.
On January 20, 2013, a game here against the cross-town rival Gee-Gees ended in a shootout.

landmarks.name: Teraanga Commons
facts: It is the residence dining hall, home to the residence association's convenience store.

landmarks.name: Richcraft Hall
facts: It houses the School of Public Policy and Administration.

landmarks.name: Rideau House
facts: It is the newest residence, opened in 2025.

landmarks.name: Steacie Building
facts: It is the chemistry building, named after a former president of the National Research Council.

landmarks.name: Nicol Building
facts: It is the home of the Sprott School of Business, designed by Hariri Pontarini Architects.
It was completed in 2021.

landmarks.name: Frontenac House
facts: It is a residence for returning second-year students.
It was added in 2008 as a sustainably designed residence hall.

landmarks.name: Lanark House
facts: It was one of the first residences, originally reserved for men while Renfrew House was for women.
